headline: AI DATA CENTER BOOM FUELS NUCLEAR RENAISSANCE — THREE STOCKS TO WATCH AS URANIUM HOLDS $88/LB
snippet: An August 7, 2026 analysis from 24/7 Wall St. identifies Cameco Corporation (NYSE: CCJ), Constellation Energy (NASDAQ: CEG), and BWX Technologies (NYSE: BWXT) as the three nuclear energy stocks best positioned to capture the AI data center power demand boom. The convergence is structural: AI hyperscalers — Google, Microsoft, Amazon — are writing multi-decade power purchase agreements for nuclear baseload, the only zero-carbon energy source with the 24/7 reliability that training clusters and inference operations demand. Cameco sells uranium fuel and has seen its stock rise nearly 50% year-over-year; Constellation Energy operates 55 gigawatts of nuclear capacity; BWXT holds an $8.65 billion backlog in nuclear components, services, and small modular reactor systems. Uranium spot prices hold at $88 per pound, up 34% year-over-year, with long-term contract prices reaching $90–$94 per pound — levels that support new mine development economics. For junior uranium investors, the hyperscaler PPA trend is the most important structural demand signal in nuclear energy in a decade: it creates 20-to-30 year visibility for reactor operators, which feeds directly into long-term uranium contracting and ultimately into development financing for junior explorers in the Athabasca Basin and Namibia.

headline: CODELCO HALTS EL TENIENTE ANDES NORTE ON SEISMIC RISK — UP TO TWO YEARS; WORLD'S LARGEST UNDERGROUND COPPER MINE
snippet: Codelco suspended all development and construction work at the Andes Norte sector of its El Teniente Division in central Chile on August 4, 2026, citing an emerging deep-seismicity phenomenon at the mine's lowest levels that behaves differently from previously managed seismic patterns. The suspension could last as long as two years according to union representatives, affecting four contractors, more than 20 contracts, and approximately 3,000 workers. Andes Norte is a critical life-extension project for El Teniente — the world's largest underground copper mine — designed to maintain long-term output; Codelco confirmed that current productive operations continue normally, but the expansion that feeds future copper supply is on hold. The pause followed six months of internal geological analysis identifying an emerging seismic phenomenon tied directly to the greater depth of the Andes Norte project — a structural challenge without a quick fix. For copper investors, a potential two-year halt at a tier-one expansion project announced in the same week as the DRC concentrate ban (see separate story) represents a compounding supply-side signal: structural copper deficits could persist through the late 2020s even as demand from electrification and AI infrastructure continues to accelerate.

headline: DRC BANS COPPER AND COBALT CONCENTRATE EXPORTS — REUTERS; IVANHOE CLARIFIES DISRUPTION IS LIMITED
snippet: The Democratic Republic of Congo banned exports of copper and cobalt concentrates in an order signed June 29, 2026 and disclosed by Reuters exclusively on August 6, 2026 — a joint ministerial directive effective immediately, with one-year strategic waivers available at the Mines Minister's discretion. Copper briefly spiked to $14,369 per metric tonne on the LME before Ivanhoe Mines Ltd. issued a clarification: DRC copper exports are overwhelmingly refined cathode (696,725 tonnes in Q1 2026), not concentrate (53,926 tonnes in Q1, containing only 18,863 tonnes of copper metal), meaning the copper concentrate ban has limited immediate practical impact. The cobalt situation is more directly affected — DRC's cobalt processing capacity is less developed than its smelter chain, making the cobalt concentrate portion of the ban more consequential for battery materials supply chains. This is the fourth iteration of DRC's domestic processing push since 2013 (after 2019 and 2023), each accompanied by waiver mechanisms. For retail mining investors, the structural direction of DRC resource policy continues to favour upstream producers in Tier-1 jurisdictions where domestic processing is already captured — and the sustained pressure on concentrate exporters raises long-term risks for miners operating under DRC concentrate sales agreements.

headline: OSISKO GOLD HITS 95.93 g/t AU OVER 4.60m AT PROSERPINE — OPEN PIT POTENTIAL; 14-FOR-14 FIRST DRILL PROGRAM (OSK)
snippet: Osisko Gold Group Inc. (TSX: OSK) reported August 5, 2026 first-ever drill results from the Proserpine regional greenfield target — located 7 kilometres from the company's permitted, 100%-owned Cariboo Gold mine in central British Columbia — with all 14 completed holes intersecting gold mineralization. Highlight hole PSP-26-004 returned 4.60 metres at 95.93 g/t gold from 110 metres depth, including a 50-centimetre interval of 873 g/t gold; hole PSP-26-001 returned 8.60 metres at 5.46 g/t gold from 77 metres vertical depth. The 14-hole program defines a mineralized footprint of 1.0 kilometre by 0.5 kilometre, open in all directions, and Osisko describes the system as consistent with open-pit mining potential alongside the planned underground Cariboo operation. Three rigs are now drilling Proserpine with expansion planned to Southeast and Northwest targets. For Cariboo investors, the Proserpine discovery adds a second deposit style — potential open pit — to a project modelled as purely underground, broadening its economic optionality significantly. A 100% hit rate across 14 exploratory holes in a new, undrilled area, including near-surface intercepts above 90 g/t gold, is among the strongest first-program validations in BC gold exploration in 2026.

headline: OUTCROP SILVER: 2,559 g/t AgEq IN 0.71m AT MORENA — SANTA ANA MRE DUE SEPTEMBER; MULTI-VEIN SYSTEM DEFINED (OCG)
snippet: Outcrop Silver & Gold Corporation (TSX: OCG, OTC: OCGSF) reported August 5, 2026 high-grade silver-gold drill intercepts from two targets at its Santa Ana Project in Huila Department, Colombia: at the Morena target, hole MOR-26-04 returned 0.71 metres at 2,559 g/t silver equivalent (1,646 g/t Ag and 10.35 g/t Au), and a second interval of 1.74 metres at 646 g/t AgEq (488 g/t Ag and 1.79 g/t Au), supporting Morena's inclusion as a third contributor to a September 2026 updated mineral resource estimate alongside the established Aguilar and Guadual vein systems. At silver above $62 per ounce, a 2,559 g/t AgEq intercept at 0.71 metres represents one of the highest silver-equivalent grades reported globally in 2026, characteristic of Colombia's high-sulphidation epithermal silver belt. For silver investors watching the development pipeline, Santa Ana is one of the few advanced high-grade silver-gold projects progressing through systematic multi-vein resource delineation with a hard delivery milestone — the September 2026 MRE will be the first to formally capture the expanded three-vein footprint assembled since 2025 and represents a near-term re-rating catalyst for investors who have followed the drill-by-drill construction of the resource.

headline: COPPER LEADS BROADER METALS REBOUND — FX EMPIRE: URANIUM EQUITIES LAG SPOT; LITHIUM TRIES TO FLOOR
snippet: FX Empire's August 2026 multi-commodity price forecast examines three metals at very different points in their cycles. Copper leads at $14,000+ per metric tonne — up 47% year-on-year — driven by record US stockpiling ahead of an expected copper import tariff, compounded this week by the El Teniente Andes Norte expansion halt and the DRC concentrate ban; the metal is pricing in structural supply deficits that physical traders have been front-running for months. Uranium presents the sector's largest fundamental dislocation: spot prices at $88 per pound are up 34% year-on-year and long-term contracts are at $90–$94 per pound, yet uranium equities (URNM) remain down year-to-date — a divergence that Sprott Asset Management has described as one of the most significant mismatches in commodity equity markets. Lithium carbonate in China stabilised at approximately CNY 142,750 per tonne in early August following a six-month decline, with Mineral Resources' Bald Hill and Core Lithium's Finniss both back in production after extended care-and-maintenance periods — a supply signal that the floor may be forming after a brutal correction from the CNY 600,000 peak. For mining investors, the three-metal snapshot illustrates why portfolio construction in 2026 matters: copper is at cycle highs, uranium equities lag their own fundamental signals, and lithium is attempting a base — each requiring a different entry thesis and risk tolerance.

headline: WESTWARD GOLD TRENCHES 13.4m AT 6.55 g/t AU NEAR BARRICK'S FOURMILE, NEVADA — DRILLING NEXT (WG)
snippet: Westward Gold Inc. (CSE: WG) announced August 4, 2026 initial assay results from the first of three planned trenches at the SSD Target at its Toiyabe Hills Property in central Nevada: a 177-metre trench returned a 34.8-metre composite averaging 2.84 g/t gold including a 13.4-metre high-grade core of 6.55 g/t gold, with individual chip samples reaching 17.90 g/t. Toiyabe Hills sits in the same structural corridor as Barrick's Fourmile project — one of the highest-grade undeveloped gold deposits in North America — in Nevada's Carlin-type gold belt. SSD is a Silicified Sediment Zone where gold is hosted in decarbonated and silicified sedimentary units along controlling fault structures — the classic Carlin-type lithological package. Two additional trenches remain to be assayed, and Westward plans to move directly from trench results to a drill program targeting the structural controls identified in this first trench. At $4,300+ gold, a 6.55 g/t surface gold zone in a proven Nevada Carlin district adjacent to a major Barrick deposit advancing to drill testing is the kind of pre-discovery setup that has historically catalysed outsized junior mining stock moves — the trench confirms grade, but it is the subsequent drill program that will determine whether this is a shallow anomaly or a depth-continuous Carlin deposit.

headline: METALSOURCE DOUBLES DOWN AT SILVER HILL — 2ND RIG TARGETS 16,604 g/t AgEq ZONE; MRE PLANNED 2027 (MSM)
snippet: Metalsource Mining Inc. (CSE: MSM) announced August 6, 2026 the launch of an expansion drill program at its Silver Hill Project in North Carolina, targeting the area surrounding hole SH26-07 — previously the project's highest-grade intercept, returning 12.62 metres at 3,786 g/t silver equivalent overall, with a 6.95-metre sub-interval of 6,730 g/t AgEq and a 2.74-metre high-grade core of 16,604 g/t AgEq (including 209.1 g/t gold). A second diamond drill rig and dedicated night-shift crew will mobilize in early August, expected to triple total drilling capacity and accelerate the project's path toward an inaugural mineral resource estimate targeted for early 2027. Silver Hill is a polymetallic epithermal vein system in a historically producing North Carolina silver-gold district, and the expansion program is designed to define lateral and down-plunge extensions of the highest-grade zone. At silver above $62 per ounce and gold above $4,300, a drill hole returning 16,604 g/t AgEq over 2.74 metres is among the highest-grade silver-equivalent intercepts reported anywhere in 2026 — grade confirmation has been achieved; the outstanding question, which the tripled drill capacity is designed to answer before the 2027 MRE deadline, is how far the high-grade zone extends in three dimensions.

headline: GOLDSEEK SWOT: DPM METALS Q2 RECORDS $227M FCF ON 103K GEO — BREVENE SOUTH 713m AT 2.52 g/t AuEq (DPM)
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT analysis for August 4–8 highlights DPM Metals Inc. (TSX/NYSE: DPM) as a standout performer in a banner gold earnings season. Q2 2026 results (reported July 30) showed record free cash flow of $227 million and adjusted net earnings of $211 million ($0.95 per share) on production of approximately 103,000 gold equivalent ounces — the company's 12th consecutive year of hitting guidance. The flagship Chelopech copper-gold mine in Bulgaria processed 549,000 tonnes at 3.03 g/t gold and 0.78% copper with all-in sustaining costs of $1,174 per GEO, generating margins that have roughly doubled year-on-year at $4,300+ gold. Running concurrently, DPM's 15,000-metre, 5-rig 2026 drilling campaign at the Brevene South Porphyry (BSP) target adjacent to Chelopech continues to expand what is already one of 2026's most extraordinary exploration intercepts: 713 metres at 2.52 g/t gold equivalent (1.31 g/t Au and 1.16% Cu) within a phyllic alteration envelope exceeding 1,000 by 1,500 metres — the scale associated with the world's largest porphyry copper-gold systems. BSP is DPM's fourth major discovery since 2023 and remains open in all directions. For investors evaluating the combination of record earnings and discovery upside at a single company, DPM's Q2 illustrates why a $1,174 AISC operation at $4,300 gold — generating $227 million in free cash flow in a single quarter — is still arguably undervalued if Brevene South proves out at the scale its alteration envelope implies.

headline: OMINECA DISCOVERS LODE GOLD AT WINGDAM — HARD ROCK ZONE 500m FROM BC PALEOPLACER; EUREKA FAULT NEXT TARGET (OMM)
snippet: Omineca Mining and Metals Ltd. (TSX-V: OMM) announced August 6, 2026 the discovery of a hard rock (lode) gold zone at its Wingdam exploration project in British Columbia's Cariboo Mining District — the first confirmation of a proximal lode gold source for the rich placer gold historically recovered from Lightning Creek. Winter 2025 drill results returned initial intercepts of 4.84 g/t gold over 1.07 metres and 1.25 g/t gold over 2.0 metres, located 500 metres west of and structurally below the existing Wingdam underground paleoplacer project, associated with ultramafic rocks and quartz-calcite veining along the Eureka Thrust Fault. The discovery reframes Wingdam from a paleoplacer recovery operation into a combined project with a hard rock lode exploration target: the existing underground infrastructure and permits that service the paleoplacer now provide direct access to investigate a potentially significant primary gold system. Future exploration will focus on the Eureka Thrust Fault corridor in the immediate vicinity of the lode discovery. For investors tracking BC gold exploration in the Cariboo Mining District — home to Osisko Gold's Cariboo Gold Project and active with multiple new drill programs in 2026 — Omineca's lode discovery confirms that district exploration is generating new deposit types, not just drilling known paleoplacer extensions.
